headline: Approved August 6 minutes and designLAB invoice for $38,430 while discussing pile cost increase of about $31,000
summary: The committee approved the 8/6/26 meeting minutes and reviewed project updates on the boathouse equipment racks, pile foundation cost changes, and project financing. The committee approved designLAB invoice 26-02.0726 for construction documents billing. The team discussed switching to timber piles after structural engineers found a miscalculation in pile load requirements.
decisions: Approved the August 6, 2026 meeting minutes, with all members voting yes except Eric Rubin who abstained since he was not present at that meeting.

Deb motioned to approve the invoice, and Amanda seconded the motion. The committee voted unanimously to approve the invoice.

Malden River Works Salt Shed & Boathouse Project Updates 
 Updates regarding boathouse discussion with Rich Whelen and Charlie Conefry.   
• A meeting was held earlier today between the designLAB team, Rich Whelen, Charlie Conefry, Deb 
Burke, Nelson Miller, and Rebekah McPheeters. The goal of the meeting was to ensure that the 
boathouse is populated with the appropriate equipment racks to accom modate the current rowing 
team as well as allow for future expansion. Sam shared that, based on this discussion, the plan is to 
set up racks for 8s and 4s. The building is designed such that the ceiling can support hanging boats, 
although no hanging hardware will be installed as part of this project.  The design will also ensure

there is space for ergs, flammable cabinets, tents, race supplies, etc. (although none of those

and design of the boathouse. 
designLAB team to present on changes to the project’s cost estimates.  
• Sam reported that, about a week ago, his team heard from their structural engineers that they had 
miscalculated the load per pile for the buildings in this project. Sam did call Rebekah McPheeters with 
this information, and at the time he thought that the cost increase could be in the neighborhood of 
$500,000.  
• Context: This project’s proposed buildings are to be built on organics and fill, which do not provide 
great support. As a result, the buildings require piles. Originally, we were planning for 50 piles for the 
boathouse, and 86 for salt shed. The piles being considered would have extenders that could reach 
greater depths to hit the clay under the organics/fill.  
• When the structural engineers flagged the problem last week, it seemed like there was need for  
almost twice as many piles (154 piles for the salt shed and 113 piles for the boathouse), which could 
double the cost of the piles.  
• The engineers worked with the geo tech to look at switching to timber piles that get driven into the 
ground. Timber piles are more expensive per pile, but they can hold more weight, so we would need 
fewer piles overall. With this plan, we would need 66 piles for the salt shed, and 65 piles for the 
boathouse. The team got a quote from a pile company that would result in a $31k increase to the 
project. Sam recommended that we add a little additional contingency to account for all of the 
variables here.  
• Steve Winslow requested a copy of the geotechnical report, as he ran into an issue like this in 
Gloucester. He recommended that the geo tech look to see if there are inlets or water underground. 
Sam agreed to provide the report and to relay the concern about variable depth to the team.  
• Sam pulled up a copy of the geotechnical report, which did not show any borings at the exact site of 
the future boathouse. Marie noted that there was another set of borings done in preparation for the 
dock, which are closer to the boathouse site. Steve recommended that the team find the USGS maps 
of the Malden River before it was straightened.  
• Nelson Miller asked if designLAB would revise their overall project cost estimate based on this new 
information. Sam shared that, while they have provided the option to conduct a second cost estimate 
for additional cost in their project proposal should the City want to pursue, they don’t see much value 
in doing so at this point.  
Updates regarding project ﬁnancing.  
• Ron Hogan shared that the Mayor’s intent is to send a paper to the City Council, recommending that 
Malden repurpose money that was borrowed for the Roosevelt Park project for this project. Amanda 
Linehan is already aware of this, as City Council President. Ron said that he will speak with Rebekah 
offline about slides for the presentation to Council.  
Invoice Approval 
 Committee to review and approve designLAB invoice 26-02.0726 (Attached). 
• Sam shared that designLAB billed 25% for Construction Documents  (CDs) in July, resulting in this 
invoice. They expect to bill another 25% in August, and then 50% in September.  
• Deb motioned to approve the invoice, and Amanda seconded the motion. The committee voted 
unanimously to approve the invoice.

to the committee when done. Then, his team will need to work with the City and the Owner’s Project

• Marie noted that their construction access plan needs to be shown to DPW and Water Department staff,

• Bekah noted that the City is planning to advertise a bid for the OPM next week.  
Adjournment  
Eric motioned to adjourn, and Steve seconded the motion. The committee voted unanimously to adjourn the
